title: Trump Sons Take Helm of Trump Organization, Eye Domestic Expansion During Presidency
description_short: Trump Sons Take Helm of Trump Organization, Eye Domestic Expansion During Presidency
description_medium: In 2017, Eric and Donald Trump Jr. took the helm of the Trump Organization and adjusted to operating during their father's presidency. description_long: In 2017, Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr. took over day-to-day leadership of the Trump Organization while their father was president. description_long: On May 16, 2025, Moody’s Ratings lowered the U.S. government’s long-term issuer rating from Aaa to Aa1 and changed its outlook to stable. description_long: In February 2025, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services cut federal funding for ACA Navigator organizations to $10 million a year, down from about $98 million. Navigators help people understand coverage options and enroll through the health-insurance marketplaces. CMS said the reduction reflected a shift toward more effective Exchange strategies. The correction attached to this entry is important: enhanced ACA premium subsidies did not expire in March 2025 and remained in effect through the end of that year. The documented event is a cut to Navigator program funding, not the end of premium tax credits. These are separate parts of ACA implementation, and conflating them would overstate the policy change. title: Trump Says Israel Should End Gaza War While Defending Its Response to October 7
description_short: Trump Says Israel Should End Gaza War While Defending Its Response to October 7
description_medium: In a March 2024 interview, Trump said he would have responded to Hamas's October 7 attack in a similar way to Israel, but also said Israel should finish the war and was losing international support. Later campaign remarks used stronger 'finish the job' language. Those later statements should not be backdated to October 8, 2023 or summarized as a single uninterrupted position of unconditional support.
description_long: In a March 2024 interview, Trump said he would have responded to Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack in a way similar to Israel, while also saying Israel should finish the war and was losing international support. Later campaign remarks used the phrase “finish the job.” The correction associated with the record warns against merging those later comments with an October 8, 2023 position or presenting Trump as having maintained one uninterrupted line of unconditional support. The distinction matters because the statements occurred at different moments in the war and included both defense of Israel’s response and pressure to conclude the conflict. This entry is about Trump’s shifting public comments, not a change in U.S. policy or an assessment of the military campaign. The supplied sources do not document how Israeli officials responded to the interview or establish what policy Trump would have enacted as president. The account preserves the chronology and the tension between his remarks.
